claims.statement: Joe Goss challenged Tom Allen, 'Champion of America', to fight under London prize ring rules for $500 to $5,000 a side and the championship of the world.
claims.excerpt: according to the rules of the London prize ring, for any amount of money ftom $500 to) $5,000 a side and the Chasaplonstia of the world.

claims.statement: Joe Goss sent $500 to Eph Holland of Cincinnati as a deposit for the match, to show he meant business.
claims.excerpt: To show that I inean business, I have this day forwanted to Mr. Eph Holland.

claims.statement: Tom Allen had repeatedly said he would never deposit money with an Eastern stakeholder, claiming foul play by certain New York parties, and wanted a Western stakeholder and a Western place for the match.
claims.excerpt: Tom has also repeatedly stated that he would never deposit any money in the hands of an Eastern stakeholder

claims.statement: Tom Allen had personal altercations with a New York paper (printed as 'Nope') and with Wilkes' Spirit of the Times, which refused to print Goss's challenge to him.
claims.excerpt: Allen has had some personal altercations both with the New York Nope and MFilkes' Spirit of the Times

quotes.speaker: Joe Goss
quotes.text: To show that I inean business, I have this day forwanted to Mr. Eph Holland.
quotes.topic: deposit to show he means business

notes: The challenge letter's date prints as 'April M4, 1876' (OCR); only the month is given. The hint's 'Clipper' is not in the text; the paper is printed as 'Nope'. The 'Cincinnati Enquirer of yesterday' is 1876-04-28. Goss's own fight record is not about Allen except the 1867 draw.
